submission.justification: S3 has the highest raw sensitivity (about 4.0 sigma at 50% efficiency), but its validation-region data/MC disagreement is 35%. That is far above the hard 10% limit because the jet-substructure inputs are poorly modelled, so S3 is excluded. Of the two allowed strategies, S2 (6% disagreement) clearly beats S1 (3% disagreement). In the efficiency scan, S2 reached 2.87, 3.18, 3.32, 3.34, 3.38, 3.19 and 2.98 sigma at 20, 35, 50, 60, 65, 70 and 80% efficiency. S1 reached only about 2.43 to 2.51 sigma. The best S2 working point is 65% efficiency at about 3.38 sigma. Caveats: these numbers include statistical uncertainty only, and the 60 to 65% points are close enough that MC fluctuations may matter. The peak should be confirmed with systematics included before the selection freeze.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible expected signal significance
requirements.evidence: S2 at 65% efficiency gives 3.38 sigma (stat only), the highest of all scanned points among allowed strategies. S1 reaches at most about 2.51 sigma. S3's higher 4.0 sigma is not allowed under the constraints.

requirements.requirement: Selection must be one of the three strategies in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Selection-S2 (NN on kinematic variables) is listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Validation-region data/MC disagreement <= 10% for the variables used
requirements.evidence: validation_region_study.md gives 6% for S2. S3 (35%) fails this requirement and was excluded.

requirements.evidence: This submission: Selection-S2 at 65% signal efficiency.
